Findings.Title: Firewall profiles
Findings.Guidance: Enable the Domain, Private and Public firewall profiles. Review effective rules separately.

Findings.Title: Microsoft Defender protection
Findings.Evidence: Defender is in Normal mode with antivirus and real-time protection enabled.
Findings.Guidance: Review Windows Security and your approved antivirus product. Passive Defender can be intentional with another antivirus; this tool does not validate that product.

Findings.Title: System drive BitLocker
Findings.Evidence: Collection failed: Synthetic example: access denied by provider.
Findings.Guidance: Review system-drive encryption and protection in BitLocker settings. Back up recovery keys securely before changing protection.

Findings.Title: User Account Control
Findings.Evidence: EnableLUA=1; admin prompt=5; secure desktop=1. A restart may be needed after policy changes.
Findings.Guidance: Review UAC policy: enable Admin Approval Mode and prompts on the secure desktop. This check does not inspect standard-user or built-in Administrator policies.

Findings.Title: Remote Desktop configuration
Findings.Evidence: Local RDP configuration allows connections with NLA. Confirm that remote access is intended and review effective policy.
Findings.Guidance: Disable Remote Desktop when unused. If needed, require NLA and review policy overrides, firewall scope and access groups. Registry settings alone do not establish network reachability.

Findings.Title: SMBv1 server protocol
Findings.Evidence: EnableSMB1Protocol=False on the SMB server; client state is not assessed.
Findings.Guidance: Disable the SMBv1 server protocol after reviewing legacy dependencies. This check covers the server configuration only; the SMBv1 client and optional feature need separate review.

Findings.Title: Built-in local Guest account
Findings.Evidence: Built-in local Guest account (RID 501) is disabled.
Findings.Guidance: Disable the built-in local Guest account unless an approved workflow explicitly requires it. Other local accounts and group memberships are outside this check.

Findings.Title: PowerShell script block logging policy
Findings.Evidence: Explicit HKLM policies: Windows PowerShell=1; PowerShell Core=0 (0 includes absent values). Other policy paths may still enable logging.
Findings.Guidance: Review script block logging for both Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7. This checks explicit HKLM policies only; HKCU settings, Core policy inheritance, log retention and event delivery are not assessed. Logged script content can contain secrets.
